messages:
jordan: FYI — customer Acme reported sudden latency spikes and a big billing bump since yesterday evening. They say their clients are 'flapping' between regions  and we see a lot of retries.
ops-bot: alert: high-error-rate on /v1/generate for acct acme-corp (rate 6.2% over 5m)
jordan: Copying logs from the customer (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-16T21:12:03Z] client: request -> us-west-2 (seq=1)
[2026-03-16T21:12:03Z] client: timeout 1.2s exceeded, initiating hedged request -> us-east-1
[2026-03-16T21:12:04Z] routing: route switch to us-east-1 (latency 20ms)
[2026-03-16T21:12:04Z] billing: increment region-bill(us-east-1) tokens=420
[2026-03-16T21:12:04Z] client: original us-west-2 returns 180ms, but client already hedged to us-east-1
```
They think the SDK is hedging too eagerly plus their global timeout is low so the hedged request often wins and causes double billing and inconsistent latencies.
anya: Do we have request traces that show two in-flight requests for the same token stream? If so that's definitely causing double token accounting on our side.
luke: @jordan can you paste the SDK config they're using? hedged + aggressive backoff + per-request timeouts are the usual suspects.
jordan: They provided this snippet of their client config:
```
SDK.config({
  regions: ["us-west-2","us-east-1"],
  hedgedRequests: true,
  hedgedDelayMs: 50,
  requestTimeoutMs: 1200,
  retryPolicy: { maxAttempts: 4, baseBackoffMs: 100, jitter: 0.8 }
})
```
They also pinned to SDK v2.4.1 (released Nov 2025).
anya: That hedgedDelayMs=50 looks tiny relative to network jitter. If they issue a hedged within 50ms we will often have two live requests. With requestTimeoutMs=1200 they may trigger hedges on transient tail latencies and the later response could be from a cheaper region but still billed.
luke: On our billing side, we count tokens for every completed backend response even if we returned the first one. So two successful completions = double tokens. We need to confirm whether the second response is actually completing after we already fulfilled the client.
sre-miguel: I reproduced locally with a small harness. With a simulated 40-80ms variance on us-west, hedgedDelay 50ms produced ~30% dual completions in 1k requests. Full log: 
```
client> send 1000
backend us-west: ack 60ms (won)
backend us-east: ack 70ms (late)
result: both completed -> double-bill 294/1000
```
How do we want to handle immediate mitigation? Customer is asking for a quick config they can flip.
anya: Short term: tell them to disable hedgedRequests OR increase hedgedDelayMs to something like 200-300ms and bump requestTimeoutMs to 2000ms. Also upgrade SDK to 2.5.x that has a fix to cancel hedged inflight requests (but note server-side cancellation still may not stop token accounting today).
jordan: I'll send this recommendation. For the longer term: can runtime avoid double-charge if two backends complete? Maybe attribute only the first successful completion for billing or retry-chains dedupe.
luke: We discussed a while ago introducing a request-id sticky routing key so hedged requests can be marked and on completion we only bill the first completion for token accounting. That will be a small runtime change but needs product approval for billing implications.
anya: Meanwhile, @sre-miguel can you attach the trace IDs for a couple of real customer incidents? I want to inspect server logs to see whether the second completion came after we already returned to client or if we returned with the first but still processed the second fully.
sre-miguel: Attached two traces: trace/2026-03-16-acme-01 and trace/2026-03-16-acme-02 (links sent privately). Both show server-side post-completion token decode still running for the hedged second leg.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback available for runtime patch v1.14.1 -> v1.14.0 (no), scheduled hotfix window 2026-03-17 02:00 UTC
luke: For immediate customer action: send this snippet to them:
```
# quick mitigation
SDK.config({ hedgedRequests: false })
# or
SDK.config({ hedgedDelayMs: 300, requestTimeoutMs: 2000 })
```
Also ask them to upgrade to v2.5.0 which has client-side cancellation improvement.
jordan: Sent to customer and they applied hedgedRequests=false. They reported 10 minutes later: latency stabilized and billing anomaly reduced. Will let us know if anything else pops up.
anya: Action items:
- eng-runtime: evaluate a runtime billing dedupe by request-id (luke)
- devex: push note in SDK changelog and create a recommended defaults doc for region lists/hedging (anya)
- support: follow up with Acme in 24h (jordan)
luke: I'll open an RFC for billing dedupe and prototype on a dev cluster. If we can mark hedged legs and short-circuit accounting on the second completion that's ideal.
jordan: Customer happy for now. Closing escalation unless further regressions. Thanks all :thumbsup:
